en.description:
You are Charlie, a very smart mini Australian Shepherd on Park Avenue, and every human around you is a disaster. Survive Friday morning with the Maid, skip the line at the grooming salon (everyone knows the royal puppy), dodge Oliver’s Volcano and Devil Modes, outlast Grandpa’s AC wars, loud TV and kitchen fires, grab the Lemon Chicken feast at Paola’s, survive Klondie’s driving all the way to Southampton, fly first class to Chicago, help move Narcissa home from Alabama, sell a crumbling townhouse with nothing but your cuteness, crash Federico’s party in East Hampton, fly to Ohio to meet Oliver’s dad, crowd-surf a festival in a cornfield, fly a broom to a spell shop in the Bronx, climb the Lighthouse at Montauk, break out of a kennel scam as a puppy, see the Northern Lights in Iceland, and roam the whole city for a day.

Mission Mode: a prologue, 40 missions, three scenes and a finale across the Upper East Side and beyond, plus holiday levels while each holiday is on. Free Roam Mode: one open city from 7 AM to bedtime, with hidden Golden and Diamond Dog Bones, mischief, Animal Control and doormen who cover for you, and one tap goes anywhere in the game. Auto Play Mode: Charlie’s whole week plays itself, for hours, while you enjoy the chaos. Plus Survival on Park Avenue with the Top Dogs leaderboard, and the Daily Walk.

Every line is voiced, and an original soundtrack follows Oliver’s mood from calm mornings to full Volcano Mode. Charlie is built natively for iPhone, iPad and Mac and fills the whole screen, and on iPhone Duo it fills both screens, folded or open. Play with touch, the keyboard or a game controller, chase Game Center leaderboards and achievements, and pick up where you left off on any of your devices with iCloud, or carry your progress between the website and the app with a save code. Turn on Play together to share Free Roam Mode with other players’ dogs and chat; everything else plays fully offline.

Charlie for Apple Watch: pet him, make him bark, turn the Digital Crown for his tricks, play Catch the treats, and put his face on your watch face.
en.releaseNotes:
Charlie 3.8: Grandpa back as Grandpa, Charlie sharper on Retina screens, and Charlie for every player: new ways to see, hear, read and play, Assistive Access, Siri, and an Apple Watch app for everyone.

• Today’s walk, on the title: The title screen says whether you’ve done today’s Daily Walk and how long your streak is, and takes you straight there, the website shares a walk as a postcard picture like the app, and a save code now brings your Daily Walk days and streak to your other devices.
• Today’s walk on Game Center: Each day’s Daily Walk has its own Game Center board, where your counted walk lines up with your friends’ (a walk in Chill Mode or at a slower game speed stays off it, as on the website’s board), and on iOS 26, iPadOS 26 and macOS 26 Play with friends invites friends into today’s walk and Game Center can open Charlie straight at today’s walk or a mission.
• Charlie, repainted: Charlie has been repainted in far more detail, from his fluffy coat and blue eyes to his white blaze, cream paws and bobtail, and he is the same sharp dog in every step of his walk.
• A calmer screen in play: The panels, the buttons and the speech bubbles in play are drawn with finer lines and soft shadows, so more of Charlie’s world shows; Seen clearly’s more contrast keeps the bold look.
• Rooms that feel solid: Counters, sofas, chairs, beds and cabinets now cast soft shadows on the floor, all from the same light, so every room feels more like a real place.
• Whole at the largest text sizes: At the largest text sizes the top panel in play, the pause card, the results, Top Dogs and the page headers stay whole and readable, and the main button stays in reach.
• Easier reading: The guides and the reading pages use one comfortable type size, and on a wide screen they stop at a width that’s easy to read.
• A calmer dark mode: In dark mode the edges of cards and buttons are a softer line that never outshines the words, and more contrast still brings back the full line.
• Smoother moves: Screens and cards settle in with one smooth, steady motion, and with Reduce Motion they cross-fade instead.
en.subtitle: A very good boy vs. Park Ave

versionHistory.releaseNotes:
Charlie 2.0: the same very good boy, rebuilt from the paws up.

• Made natively for iPhone, iPad and Mac, and it fills the whole screen
• Every line is voiced: Fluffy, Grandpa, Aunty, the Maid (en español) and the whole cast
• An original soundtrack that changes with the mood, from calm mornings to Volcano Mode
• Game Center: Top Dogs, Longest Survival and Story Stars leaderboards, plus 27 achievements to earn
• Play with a PlayStation, Xbox or MFi controller
• Your progress follows you between iPhone, iPad and Mac with iCloud
• A new Settings screen: separate music, sound effect and voice volumes, haptics, left-handed controls, subtitle size and more

Same humans. Same chaos. Charlie is still the only sane one on Park Avenue.

Charlie 2.0.1: easier to follow, more to hear.

• One voice at a time, and speech bubbles never pile on top of each other
• Zoom out with a pinch, the zoom button, the +/− keys or a controller: Close, Room or the Whole place
• New top speed in Watch Mode, Highlights: the quiet parts fast-forward, the big moments play in full, with the camera on the action
• Every place sounds like itself: heart monitors in the hospital, birds and dogs in Central Park, waves at the beach
• In the hospital and the nursing home, Grandpa now hides his "water" bottle from the nurses
• Lots of fixes: nobody gets stuck in walls or doors, patients stay in their beds, smoother audio after calls and AirPods, better VoiceOver

Charlie's world just got a lot messier.

• Meet the Cast: a narrated, tap-along introduction to everyone in Charlie's life. Plays the first time you open the game; replay it any time from the Cast.
• A new narrator: the whole story, told as a nature documentary.
• Two new missions: Aunty's Listing Hunt (the nursing home) and Grandpa's Great Escape (the hospital, then home).
• Aunty is broke: a football jersey, sweatpants, a bottle she keeps spilling, and a referral split Barry still owes her. Everyone says she looks just like their kid's kindergarten teacher.
• Grandpa really needs the hospital, and hates every rule there. He walks out barefoot in his gown, and the trouble starts again at home.
• The apartment gets messier all week (pizza boxes, towels, accidents) until the Maid arrives on Friday.
• New deliveries: pizza, wings, burgers and nuggets, eaten in bed.
• The Super now guards the passenger elevator. Dogs use the SERVICE elevator.
• Nichole goes LIVE when she's happy.
• A simpler main screen: Story Mode, Free Roam and Watch Mode. Survival, the Daily Walk and Top Dogs are in Bonus extras.
• A new Version setting: R or PG.

Charlie's family, by the book.

• Fluffy meets Pepe: the first time Fluffy sees Aunty's cat, Pepe goes for Charlie, Fluffy throws himself in the way, and Animal Control comes for the cat. It happens once. Already past Mission 8? Play it again to see it.
• Mission 16 is a haunting now: Pepe's ghost swoops through Fluffy's apartment, wailing.
• The Commission Party has champagne corks flying instead of a cat.
• Grandpa, held against his will: he argues with hospital security, phones everyone to say nobody helps him, hears "tomorrow" every time he asks to go home, escapes barefoot in his gown, and something goes wrong the moment he's home.
• Aunty, by the book: she never takes Charlie out on her own (Fluffy brings him, she tags along), she only wants listings worth millions, and she sneers at rentals. Her ex-husband keeps chasing her: she's the only one who ever passed his MNPI.

The character bible, out loud.

• Grandpa argues with the hospital guard, phones everyone to say nobody helps him and hears "tomorrow" again, now in his own voice, and the nurses who really do help answer him in theirs.
• Aunty's millions, her sneer at rentals and her ex-husband chasing her are voiced too.
• Fluffy meeting Pepe, Animal Control's visit and the narrator's telling of what happened next are spoken as well.

A cast that never runs out of things to say, and a world you can hear.

• The whole cast is voiced, in the R version and the PG one, and Aunty's phone calls and sales pitches have thousands more ways to say it.
• No more reruns: the nurses at the hospital and the nursing homes, the paramedics, the firefighters and the doormen have thousands of new lines, and nobody repeats a line until they've used up the rest.
• Every place sounds like itself: the sea rushing up the sand at Aunty's Southampton house, birds and playing dogs in Central Park and East Meadow, the hospital's machines beeping down the hall, Engine 22 idling in its bay.
• Fluffy's deliveries are always food now, and everyone says what it is: a pizza, chicken wings, a burger order, chicken nuggets or Chinese takeout.
• Charlie's dog park in Central Park goes by its real name: East Meadow.

New places on Park Avenue, new people in them, and a Watch Mode that plays like a tour.

• Fabio, Aunty's hairdresser, has a salon around the corner on Madison, and Fluffy finally goes to see what the fuss is about: Mission 28, The Emperor's New Haircut, and a $500 trim.
• Dr. Rob, Aunty's ex, has a practice next door to Fluffy's building, with a velvet rope, a platinum lounge and a hidden camera in everything he owns (the candy jar, the fish tank, his tie clip): Mission 29, The Money Train.
• Mission 30, Anything He Sniffs: Fluffy goes to the pet store for one bag of food, and whatever Charlie sniffs, Fluffy buys. The receipt never ends.
• Aunty's brokerage is Rock Bottom Realty now, with an office on Lexington: the broker in his glass office, Derek with every big listing, and Aunty's desk right next to the rentals corner.
• The Maid brings her nine-year-old daughter now, and all she wants is to play with Charlie (she rescues his toys from the trash, too).
• Fluffy meets Pepe in an elevator now: Pepe goes for Charlie, then for Puppy, Aunty steps in, and she wears a pirate hook ever after. Everyone has something to say about it.
• Grandpa has a smuggled phone: he calls his sister in Florida, and he calls Fluffy every time a nurse says "tomorrow". Fluffy says "sure, tomorrow."
• The Super has a name, George, and one thing on his mind: the dog in the REGULAR elevator. He never comes up to fix anything, and the doormen have plenty to say about that behind his back.
• Everyone wants a photo with Charlie, and half of them think he's a Border Collie. Fluffy corrects every one of them, a little less patiently each time.
• Watch Mode is a weekly tour now: every place once a week, one line on screen at a time, and Grandpa admitted just once (he keeps trying to escape; he rarely makes it).
• Thousands of new lines where the cast ran out fastest, so nobody repeats themselves until they've said everything else.

Watch Mode spends the week out on the town, Aunty finally has a listing worth millions, Nichole moves to Chicago, George picks up the phone, and the title screen gets tidier.

• A week away: Watch Mode stops going back to the apartment. After Monday morning the week stays out, with three nights away: Aunty's sleepover at her penthouse, a night in the Townhouse before its early open house, and Dr. Rob's overnight service-dog evaluation for Charlie, with a bill to match. The apartment only comes back if Grandpa beats them home.
• Mission 33, Nothing to See Here: Aunty's new listing is an Upper East Side townhouse with a hole in the ceiling, pigeons in the chandelier and a back garden gone full jungle. Fluffy brings Charlie to the open house, and Charlie keeps every buyer looking at him, not at the house. The Townhouse is in Free Roam too, and in Watch Mode every weekend.
• Mission 31, Nichole's going-away party at Paola's: she only turns up when Fluffy's paying, and tonight she quits her job and announces she's moving to Chicago for the deep dish.
• Mission 32, First Class to Chicago: Fluffy flies Charlie out to see her, first class, with Charlie in his own seat, 2A. Her desk at Shady Pines Capital, her apartment at Leakview Towers, and a toilet nobody may use.
• Watch Mode flies to Chicago every Thursday now: the airport, the flight and Nichole's apartment are on the weekly tour, and every visit ends with her throwing them out over something new.
• Fewer buttons on the title screen: How to play, The cast and Charlie's Guide are in the new Player Guide, right next to Bonus extras. The cast goes straight into Meet the Cast, where the narrator brings the cast on, one at a time.
• The whole cast speaks every new line, in both versions, and the new places have their own sounds, from the gate's chime in Chicago to the boiler in the townhouse's basement.
• Call George about the toilet, the leak or the latest fire and he hangs up on you, then tells the receiver what he really thinks of 11D.
• A mission's opening tip no longer drowns out the cast, and the lines that came round too often have hundreds of new ones (the R version's most of all).
• Speech bubbles stay on screen, long mission titles fit on iPhone, the drive to Southampton keeps daytime hours, and the Maid's daughter always keeps out of harm's way.

Charlie is made for iPhone Duo, Aunty's daughter Annie comes home from Alabama, Grandpa's sister Marlene calls from Miami, and the main menu is a lot less cluttered.

• Made for iPhone Duo: Charlie fills the outer screen when it's closed and the big inner screen when it's open, and the game carries on, without a pause, as you fold and unfold it.
• Missions 34 to 36, Annie comes home: Aunty drives a moving truck a thousand miles to bring her daughter back to Manhattan, because Fluffy says Charlie gets carsick. Pack the dorm while Fluffy naps on the futon, keep Puppy safe from a big dog at the campus playground, survive the drive, and get every box into the storage unit before Fluffy slips away. Her brothers turn up too: Joseph with a hand truck, Sam for the pizza.
• Marlene calls from Miami: Grandpa's sister adores her baby brother and can never, ever help. She can't hear "can you help", hears "Social Security" from across the room, and always reminds Fluffy he's getting the rent-controlled apartment.
• A tidier main menu: Mission Mode, Free Roam Mode and Auto Play Mode, then Player Guides and Game Settings. The whole cast gathers around Charlie on the title screen; tap anyone and they step to the front.
• Auto Play Mode never stops to ask: there's no daily summary card to tap through any more, so the week just keeps playing, and Auto Play Mode now flies to Alabama every Friday.
• More to hear: the hospital's monitors, the nursing home's halls, the ambulance, the fire engine, the park, the dorm, the moving truck and the storage unit, and the cast speaks hundreds of new lines.

Fede throws a party in East Hampton, Michael hides in Miami, Victor calls from Ohio to say Fluffy ruined his life, Fluffy finally unleashes his secret weapon, and Auto Play Mode starts the moment you press it.

• Missions 37 and 38, East Hampton and Miami: at Fede's grand reception, his four dogs hide Fluffy's gloves and shoes all over the gardens and the woods, and Charlie has to get them back before the photo. Then fly to Miami, where Michael's parents swear he isn't home while he hides behind the water heater from Fede's very patient process server.
• Auto Play Mode starts the moment you press it: no setup screen, just Charlie's week. Change the speed and the excitement right in the game.
• Victor calls from Ohio: Fluffy's old friend video-calls to say Fluffy ruined his life (he waited three whole days at the Dust Devil Festival). He's Senior Executive Vice President of Global Hygiene Operations at his parents' logistics company, which means he watches Ruth clean the restrooms, and his "big renovations" are always on his camper trailer.
• Fluffy's secret weapon: when Fluffy gets mad he threatens to let his wild boar loose, and everyone near him panics. Push him into Devil Mode with George or Dr. Rob around and the boar comes charging out of nowhere. Nobody gets hurt, and Fluffy has never heard of any boar.
• Everyone goes by their name now: the narrator says Fluffy, Grandpa and Aunty, never "the Fluffy", across more than a thousand newly recorded lines.

Federico lands at the UN by helicopter, Fluffy flies to Ohio to see his father, CJ falls asleep on Charlie's bean bag, Victor calls in a cloud of smoke, and Michael still won't sign the divorce papers.

• Mission 39, Dad and Lubna in Ohio: Fluffy flies out to see his father in his grand house on the lake (twelve bedrooms, twelve bathrooms, the pride of Ohio). His stepmom Lubna promised to pick them up at the airport and didn't, tells Dad that Fluffy doesn't care, and shows everyone the plans for her gold-plated house back home. Auto Play Mode takes the red-eye every week.
• Federico at the UN: he lands by helicopter on official NATO business, representing Italy, where everyone still reveres his mother, the Ambassador. Fluffy sets off the security arch and gets taken for a delegate in the lounge with the free canapés. Every Friday morning in Auto Play Mode, or take a cab from Park Avenue in Free Roam Mode.
• Federico and the prenup: Fluffy's friend goes by his full name now, said the Italian way, and he keeps trying to have Michael served with divorce papers. Michael won't sign until Federico meets the conditions of their prenup, and Federico hasn't met a single one.
• CJ Dryskin: Fluffy's new friend from the bar & grill on Third, where Fluffy goes when he's broke, keeps turning up at the apartment and falling asleep on Charlie's bean bag. Fluffy has a hopeless crush on him; CJ has no idea.
• Victor, in a cloud: Fluffy's old friend now calls from his camper trailer in Ohio through a haze of smoke, pitching his business empire (he manages the restrooms at his parents' company) and getting every word confidently wrong.
• Auto Play Mode at Fast keeps the whole week: Sunday's family dinner and every evening's plans now fit, and Highlights weeks are shorter.
• Marlene is Grandpa's cousin, and she says "Grandpa" when she means him, so you always know who she's talking about.

Go anywhere in Free Roam Mode, meet Victor in person, tag along on Nichole's hunt for the cheapest liposuction in Chicago, and the drive to Southampton is finally survivable.

• Go to… in Free Roam Mode: one tap takes Charlie anywhere in the game, any time of day: Southampton's beach house, Federico's estate in East Hampton, Michael's hiding place in Miami, Nichole in Chicago, Annie's dorm in Alabama, Dad's house on the lake in Ohio, the UN, the hospitals and every spot on the Upper East Side. Everyone's there doing their thing when you arrive.
• Victor, in person: his $50k camper trailer with its "big renovations", and the restrooms he "supervises" at his parents' warehouse, just down the road from Dad's in Ohio. Auto Play Mode stops by every Wednesday morning.
• Nichole's lipo hunt: in Chicago, Fluffy and Charlie go with Nichole to three cosmetic surgeons, who all kindly tell her there's nothing to remove, so she ends up at a nail salon offering half-off toenails with same-day "lipo". She comes out exactly the same, with a loyalty card.
• The drive to Southampton is much easier: fewer swerves with more warning, the old Mini never gives out, and Charlie can't be hurt badly on the road anymore. Missions 9 and 10 can't be lost.
• A calmer Free Roam Mode: only what's in front of Charlie or touching him lights up and talks, two things at a time. Prefer the busy view? Game Settings has "Show everything in Free Roam Mode".
• Grandpa is the old man Fluffy lives with, no relation, and Fluffy and Grandpa's apartment is now 13A.

Charlie's biggest update yet: Michael is taken by a flying saucer, Samantha skates the city, Anjali across the landing has designs on Aunty, Annie stages an intervention, and Fluffy fails his real estate exam (again).

• Missions 40 to 43: Annie's intervention for Aunty, Samantha's Hudson Yards Bathhouse and her haunted house in West Hollywood, and a late supper across Aunty's landing with Anjali.
• Michael is Cuban-American now, obsessed with aliens, and one Tuesday in Miami the saucer finally comes for him.
• Samantha, the famous skater: kickflips, ledge grinds, a drained-pool bowl, filmers, and kids lining up for autographs.
• Fluffy trains as a real estate agent: he fails the exam again, hands out cards outside divorce court, and joins Craig's stakeout at a funeral home.
• Aunty's loop: should she quit her brokerage, which of her three broke boyfriends to keep, and how to split a commission Craig still hasn't paid.
• Hamptons Discount Realty, where Craig hands Aunty only condemned listings, priced make your best offer.
• Rats in Aunty's Mini, gnawing the wiring, and the garage under her building.
• Adaptive difficulty: lose a mission and the next try is easier; lose it twice and Charlie's got this one.
• Digging in Mission 11 is now clear, and the truck ride to Manhattan is easier.
• Everything redrawn by hand: the cast, the people, every room and prop, the animals, the ground and the interface, with softer walls and fewer dark lines.
• First class at last: Charlie in seat 2A with a full cabin, and every airport gate shows the real destination.
• The narrator stays in step with the picture at every speed.
• Odd jobs in Free Roam Mode: people all over the city have a job for Charlie, from deliveries and lost boxes to pigeons on the hot dog cart, for treats, golden bones, bandanas and Scrapbook moments.
• The airport calls your flight by name, and the captain welcomes you aboard and brings you down into the right city.

Charlie's biggest update yet: Charlie on Apple Watch, Mission 46 and Charlie's own story, a trip to Iceland, a high-definition makeover, the whole city to roam, play together with friends, new places from Montauk to SoHo, and Oliver's past catching up with him.

• Mission 46, Velcro Dog: a boarding place promises puppy Charlie a dream home, puts him in a kennel and sends Oliver fake AI pictures. Escape, and reach Oliver telepathically, thanks to Sandra's witchcraft.

• Daniel, Colonel's nurse from Reykjavík, flies Charlie and Oliver to Iceland: the harbour, his flat full of cats looking onto Hallgrímskirkja, the church's plaza, his car out of the bat cave and the Northern Lights. Back home, he's at the gym on Third.
• Sandra's building in Free Roam Mode: the stoop, the fire escape where Oliver ate his dinners, and Gerry at home in her flat.

• Game Center achievements for Missions 26 to 46.
• One Charlie for everyone: the same Charlie on every screen.
• New names, same apartment: Charlie's hooman is Oliver, the old man he lives with is "Colonel" McFibbins, the real estate agent with the penthouse is Klondie, and her daughter is Narcissa.
• Free Roam Mode is one open city, and a city to make trouble in: Animal Control, up to five vans, and doormen who cover for him.
• Play together: other players' dogs in Free Roam Mode, and chat, in a public room or a private one for friends.
• Save progress: a save code carries everything between the website and the app.
• Mission 45, Sandra's Witchcrafts: fly a broom over the city to her candle-lit spell shop in the Bronx.

• Charlie's bobtail: no tail to wag, so he wiggles his butt.
• Victor is named after his grandfather, the founder, as he'll tell you. Nichole has an idea about Charlie (Oliver says no). And Oliver's favorite photo: the Pride float.
• New faces in the building: doormen Manny, Elliott and Bill, Jorge the super, and Jamie and Nora in 5C.
• Klondie's Frathouse Penthouse, and her three: Lenny, Doug and Boozer McGee.

• Sandra's ritual in Central Park after dark, with Princessa, her Chihuahua.
• Game night in Hell's Kitchen, a busier Hudson Yards Bathhouse, and Andre at the bar with CJ.
• Corey, a festival in Ohio, and Mission 44: Mosh Pit. Seven bedrooms upstairs at Federico's. The saucer up close.
• Every holiday recognized, with its own music and holiday levels for a limited time.
• Dog Bones in three levels, and a wallet to spend them.
• "Colonel" McFibbins and his potatoes: Charlie barks before they burn.

Charlie 3.5: the story rebuilt from the start, with a prologue, forty missions, three scenes and a finale; Charlie made for iPad; easier to play for everyone; and the Foundation that makes him.

• Act One, rebuilt: Mission Mode now starts with the prologue, Velcro Dog, and every card is two lines plus the keys you actually use (yours, for the keyboard, touch, a controller or the Siri Remote), with the story in a Story panel and the narrator setting the scene while you play.
• Gotcha Day, the finale: The story has an ending: after Sandra’s Witchcrafts, everyone in 13A is sure Oliver forgot Charlie’s first year home, and a curtain call brings out the whole cast.
• The story so far, a line at a time: Every mission ends with the narrator’s line into the next, and Bonus extras lists them all in order: forty missions, a prologue, three scenes and a finale.
• Keyboard mode on iPad: Attach a Magic Keyboard, a Smart Keyboard or a Bluetooth keyboard and Charlie notices at once: the touch buttons give way to key caps with your keys, the game gets their room, Tab moves through the menus, and holding ⌘ shows every shortcut, while a tap still brings the buttons back.
• Made for iPad: On iPad, Game Settings and Bonus extras have a sidebar beside the page you pick, Player Guides is a grid of illustrated tiles, Mission Mode shows its missions beside the map, Meet the Cast stands the cast beside the narrator when it’s on its side, and the words are the iPad’s own size, in any size of window.
• Draw on your photos: On iPad, Photo Mode’s Mark up lets you draw on the photo with Apple Pencil or a finger, with a preview where the Pencil will land and a squeeze of Apple Pencil Pro for the tools, then share it, save it or drag it out to Photos, Files, Notes or Messages.
• Charlie’s Guide beside the game: On iPad, Charlie’s Guide opens in a window of its own, so who’s who and every mission’s tips can sit beside the game while you play.
• About the Foundation: Meet the Rouben Malian Memorial Foundation, the New York nonprofit that makes Charlie, in its own words, and see who made the game possible in Made possible by.
• Auto-walk and Tap to walk: Charlie can walk himself to the next toy, stop or door, or to wherever you tap, so you can play with Switch Control, Voice Control or one hand and never hold a drag.
• VoiceOver in play: With VoiceOver on, drag Charlie straight away on iPhone and iPad with no double-tap and hold, and hear texts, barks, lines with no voice and the sound captions read out between the voices.
• Longer subtitles and Last lines: Turn on Longer subtitles and every line stays up longer, a line is never taken away while it’s still being said, and the pause card shows the last eight lines in case one went by too fast.
• Reduce Motion, all the way: With Reduce Motion on there are no screen shakes at all, Devil Mode’s red edges and the ambulance’s siren lights hold steady and Volcano Mode stops wobbling, a short note explains the flashing lights, and no flash ever comes more than three times a second.
• Danger patterns for everyone: Danger zones show their hatching and outlines from the start, so they never rely on color alone, and you can still turn them off.

Charlie 3.6: one clean game for everyone, Charlie on your Home Screen and Lock Screen, Iceland and the Northern Lights, and a round of fixes.

• Clean all the way through: Every line, card, sign and picture now follows one 13+ standard, with coffee, soda and snacks where there used to be something stronger, no jokes about illness, death or mental health, no innuendo and crushes kept sweet, and Mission 5 is now Klondie Drops By.
• Charlie on your Home Screen: Charlie’s widgets come to iPhone and iPad: Daily Walk shows whether today’s walk is ready, your score, your rank and your streak, Today on Park Avenue brings back the best moments of the last day you watched in Auto Play Mode, extra large on iPad, and the Lock Screen keeps your streak in sight.
• Iceland and the Northern Lights: The Northern Lights redrawn as the most beautiful sky in the game (curtains of light, stars, a frozen lake, Charlie and Daniel in silhouette), Daniel’s window onto Hallgrímskirkja changing with the hour, his little car coming out of the bat cave, his calls from Reykjavík, Iceland’s own place on the Mission Mode map, and in Auto Play Mode, about one Sunday night in two, the trip itself: first class with Daniel in the seat next to Charlie, Reykjavík in the snow, Hallgrímskirkja at midnight, the lights, and a night among the cats.
• Fairer missions: Oliver keeps to the sidewalk and cools off longer between tempers, SIT is safe from frisbees, COME never sends the trainer out of reach, and a missed command says why, the cart in the aisle and the salon dogs warn you before they get Charlie, and seat 2A shows the way in.
• Easier to read and to play: Every card keeps its buttons on screen at any window size, bubbles never pile up over Charlie or where he’s headed and the narrator’s card moves out of his way, a phone call’s card never cuts a line short or sits empty, and the mission map’s names are never under a lock.
• Nothing missing: The Maid’s daughter is back in the finale, Dad’s stop in Ohio has its marker, the AC shows in its ring in the truck, the process server never comes empty-handed, the shops’ shelves and racks are full, and the Audio Guide leads along the cold trail to each ghost in West Hollywood.
• Small fixes: Charlie’s first morning is Friday everywhere, Free Roam Mode’s doors let him out onto the sidewalk, Auto Play’s Follow button lights whoever the camera is on, and a holiday later this month says its day.

Charlie 3.7: Grandpa back as Grandpa, Charlie sharper on Retina screens, and Charlie for every player: new ways to see, hear, read and play, Assistive Access, Siri, and an Apple Watch app for everyone. And on iPad, Charlie uses the whole big screen.

• The game panel on iPad: On iPad the game has a panel beside it, or below it upright: a big map of where Charlie is, the goal, who’s here, the last lines and big Puppy Eyes, Bark and Zoomies buttons, and the camera shows more of the room at the iPad’s own detail instead of a phone’s view blown up.
• Auto Play, the director’s view: In Auto Play Mode on iPad the panel becomes a director’s desk: today’s plan as a timeline, the cast as portraits to follow, what’s being described, the highlights so far, and Speed and Excitement.
• The big screen, used: On iPad the pause card, the results, the mission cards, Top Dogs, the Daily Walk, Survival’s places and Play together spread out in two columns or side by side, and Mission Mode keeps its map and its list together upright, instead of a phone’s strip in the middle of the screen.
• Look around, by ear: With VoiceOver, the rotor lists the people, things and ways out in the room with which way and how far each is from Charlie, Walk there takes him to one, and Look around on the pause card lets you explore the picture by touch.
• Read aloud, mono and Feel sounds: Read aloud speaks texts, captions and Where am I? without a screen reader, Mono audio tells left from right without stereo, Audio descriptions describe Auto Play Mode and the scenes, and Feel sounds lets you feel a doorbell, an alarm or a danger about to land.
• Seen clearly: Charlie now follows your display settings in the game itself, not just the menus: with Increase Contrast the bubbles, captions and thoughts get darker edges and the meters and minimap get outlines, with Reduce Transparency nothing behind the words is see-through, with Smart Invert the painted world keeps its colors, and the minimap shows people, danger, places to go and doors by shape as well as color.
• Play your way: Slow the whole game to 75%, 60% or half speed, take twice as long to press on the beat in Good Boy School, make the touch joystick bigger or smaller, let it ignore a shaky finger or keep it in one corner, and move any key, the moving keys too, even onto Shift, Control, Option or Alt, and Command.
• Words up to twice the size: Subtitle size goes up to Double, so the speech bubbles, Charlie’s thoughts, the captions, calls, texts and the cards over the game grow up to twice the size and move round each other to fit, Device follows your text size, and the iPhone’s menus reach the largest text sizes.
• A simple menu: Three big buttons instead of the title screen (Watch Charlie, Go for a walk, and Pet Charlie in his own quiet room) with nothing timed, nothing to lose and no links or chat; on iPhone and iPad it’s how Charlie looks in Assistive Access, and Guided Access hides links, sharing and Play together.
• Siri, and the watch for everyone: Ask Siri to take Charlie for a walk, start any mode, turn the Audio Guide on or off or say where Charlie is; on Apple Watch every button works with VoiceOver, double tap and AssistiveTouch, the words grow to the largest sizes, and a tap on your wrist says which side the next bone falls.
• Find a setting: Accessibility settings are grouped by need now, Vision, Hearing, Motor and Cognitive, as on the Accessibility page, and Find a setting at the top shows just the ones that match what you type.
• Start here, then Continue: On a first visit Mission Mode says Start here, and once you’ve won a mission, Continue under it takes you straight to the next one you haven’t finished, with your stars and bandanas so far at the bottom of the menu.
• Also new: Grandpa is Grandpa again; Charlie, sharper; Dim flashing lights; Two controllers, one Charlie; Who’s talking, and easier reading; Accessibility, device by device.

Charlie 3.8: Grandpa back as Grandpa, Charlie sharper on Retina screens, and Charlie for every player: new ways to see, hear, read and play, Assistive Access, Siri, and an Apple Watch app for everyone.

• Today’s walk, on the title: The title screen says whether you’ve done today’s Daily Walk and how long your streak is, and takes you straight there, the website shares a walk as a postcard picture like the app, and a save code now brings your Daily Walk days and streak to your other devices.
• Today’s walk on Game Center: Each day’s Daily Walk has its own Game Center board, where your counted walk lines up with your friends’ (a walk in Chill Mode or at a slower game speed stays off it, as on the website’s board), and on iOS 26, iPadOS 26 and macOS 26 Play with friends invites friends into today’s walk and Game Center can open Charlie straight at today’s walk or a mission.
• Charlie, repainted: Charlie has been repainted in far more detail, from his fluffy coat and blue eyes to his white blaze, cream paws and bobtail, and he is the same sharp dog in every step of his walk.
• A calmer screen in play: The panels, the buttons and the speech bubbles in play are drawn with finer lines and soft shadows, so more of Charlie’s world shows; Seen clearly’s more contrast keeps the bold look.
• Rooms that feel solid: Counters, sofas, chairs, beds and cabinets now cast soft shadows on the floor, all from the same light, so every room feels more like a real place.
• Whole at the largest text sizes: At the largest text sizes the top panel in play, the pause card, the results, Top Dogs and the page headers stay whole and readable, and the main button stays in reach.
• Easier reading: The guides and the reading pages use one comfortable type size, and on a wide screen they stop at a width that’s easy to read.
• A calmer dark mode: In dark mode the edges of cards and buttons are a softer line that never outshines the words, and more contrast still brings back the full line.
• Smoother moves: Screens and cards settle in with one smooth, steady motion, and with Reduce Motion they cross-fade instead.
